R120 101.title: General Biology
R120 101.description: Biological principles cover animal and plant anatomy, physiology and ecology through lecture, laboratory and discussion.
R120 101.rationale: The actual first course in the published sequence studies biological structures, functions and ecosystems; its primary subject is life science.

R120 102.title: General Biology
R120 102.description: Biological principles cover cells, genetics and evolution through lecture, laboratory and discussion.
R120 102.rationale: The actual second course in the published sequence studies cellular processes, inheritance and evolution; its primary subject is life science.

R216 109.title: Green Planet
R216 109.description: Basic botany and plant science are applied to ecology, conservation, food, drugs, horticulture and agriculture.
R216 109.prerequisites: Not open to majors or to those who have taken or plan to take 21:120:101-102.
R216 109.rationale: The actual content is plant science and its domain applications, not AI or computer-science methods.

R216 110.title: Green Planet Laboratory
R216 110.description: Laboratory studies examine plant tissues, cells, diversity, photosynthesis, respiration and hormones.
R216 110.prerequisites: Pre- or corequisite: 21:216:109. Not open to majors or to those who have taken or plan to take 21:120:101, 102.
R216 110.rationale: The actual laboratory work studies biological plant structures and processes.

R216 205.title: Foundations of Biology: Ecology and Evolution Lecture
R216 205.description: Ecology and evolution cover populations, communities, ecosystems, species interactions and evolutionary mechanisms.
R216 205.prerequisites: Prerequisite: 21:120:200 with a grade of C or better. Corequisite: 21:216:206.
R216 205.rationale: Mathematical population models are components of a primarily biological ecology/evolution course; the overall subject is life science.

R216 206.title: Foundations of Biology: Ecology and Evolution Lab
R216 206.description: An ecology and evolution laboratory develops experiments, data collection, analysis and scientific communication.
R216 206.prerequisites: Prerequisite: 21:120:200 with a grade of C or better. Corequisite: 21:216:205.
R216 206.rationale: The actual laboratory applies scientific methods to ecological and evolutionary investigations; general analysis does not establish a separate computing or mathematics focus.

R460 103.title: Planet Earth
R460 103.description: Earth science examines the interactions of solid earth, water and atmosphere and associated resource and environmental problems.
R460 103.rationale: The actual description centers physical geology and environmental earth science.

R460 104.title: Planet Earth Laboratory
R460 104.description: Geology laboratory work identifies earth materials and interprets landforms and earth processes using maps, imagery and field visits.
R460 104.rationale: The actual exercises develop geological observation and interpretation rather than computing infrastructure or algorithms.

R460 206.title: Environmental Geology
R460 206.description: Environmental geology examines pollution, groundwater, weather, slope stability and natural hazards in urban and suburban settings.
R460 206.rationale: The actual subject is physical environmental geology and mitigation practice.

R460 207.title: Environmental Geology Laboratory
R460 207.description: Hands-on environmental geology exercises examine groundwater, soil and air pollution, slope stability, weather and earthquakes.
R460 207.rationale: The actual laboratory applies geoscience methods to environmental processes.

R830 101.title: Principles of Psychology
R830 101.description: Introductory psychology combines historical and scientific methods with neural processes, perception and cognition.
R830 101.prerequisites: Note: 21:830:101 and 102 may be taken simultaneously or in either order.
R830 101.rationale: The broad introduction combines biological and cognitive domain science with historical and methodological foundations; this bounded description does not establish a single narrower taxonomy subject.

R830 102.title: Principles of Psychology
R830 102.description: Introductory psychology combines development, personality, social influences, abnormal behavior and therapy.
R830 102.prerequisites: Note: 21:830:101 and 102 may be taken simultaneously or in either order.
R830 102.rationale: The broad introduction spans social and personality inquiry and clinical/therapeutic domain practice without a dominant subject allocation.

R920 201.title: Introduction to Sociology
R920 201.description: Sociological concepts and theories explain culture, socialization, inequality and institutions through critical analysis and examples.
R920 201.rationale: The actual description centers social structures, institutions, inequality and their effects on people and groups.
